chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.الطَّمَعُ: Greed or insatiable desire for worldly gain

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of greed according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies greed (al-ṭamaʿ) not merely as a vice, but as a state of permanent bondage, contrasting it with the spiritual liberty sought in Shia ethics. This teaching underscores the Sufi-like concept that while material wealth may enslave the body, insatiable desire enslaves the soul, a theme deeply resonant with the concept of 'abd al-nafs' (servant of the self). It serves as a practical warning against the internalization of worldly attachment, which obstructs the path to divine proximity.
